Name: reasoning_scaffold_collapse
Title: When Reasoning Becomes a Vestige: Tracing the Formation of an Internalized-Answer Circuit Across RL Training
Short Hypothesis: As a reasoning model is fine-tuned, its verbal chain-of-thought progressively decouples from the computation that actually produces the answer: an 'internalized-answer' representation forms and sharpens across checkpoints, committing to the correct answer earlier and earlier (in fewer reasoning tokens) even as the visible CoT stays long. Overthinking is the residual verbal scaffold left behind after this internal circuit has already formed. This decoupling is measurable checkpoint-by-checkpoint, its onset predicts when a CoT can be safely shortened, and it can be located as a latent-answer direction whose emergence is traceable to the training stage.
Related Work: Prior work observes, behaviorally, that reasoning tokens expand-peak-contract during fine-tuning (Scaling Competence, Shrinking Reasoning 2025), that an optimal CoT length shrinks as capability grows (When More is Less 2025; CoT-Space 2025), that RL compresses exploratory paths and optimizes a sparse subset of tokens (Towards a Mechanistic Understanding survey 2026; Reshaping Reasoning 2025), and that base models already contain reasoning mechanisms that post-training merely learns to deploy at the right time (Base Models Know How, Thinking Models Learn When 2025; AdaptThink, AutoThink, SAGE, JET 2025). All of these are either purely behavioral (token-count curves, accuracy-length tradeoffs) or intervene with RL objectives to shorten CoT. None traces, at the representational level and across training checkpoints, WHEN and HOW an internalized-answer signal forms that makes the verbal CoT redundant. Our contribution is a Formation-Tracing + Location account: we treat the latent answer-commitment as an internal component, measure the checkpoint at which it emerges and how early-in-CoT it fires, and show overthinking is the widening gap between an increasingly-early internal commitment and a slowly-shrinking verbal trace. This reframes existing behavioral observations as the surface signature of a locatable, forming internal circuit, and is distinct from all my prior single-checkpoint proposals (which read signals in one fixed model).
Abstract: Reasoning language models produce long chains of thought, and it is widely observed that reasoning length expands then contracts during fine-tuning while accuracy keeps rising. We ask a mechanistic, training-time question that the behavioral literature leaves open: as training proceeds, does an internal answer-commitment signal form that makes the visible chain of thought increasingly vestigial? We hypothesize that fine-tuning grows and sharpens an internalized-answer representation which commits to the correct answer earlier and earlier within the reasoning trace, so that overthinking becomes the residual verbal scaffold left after this internal circuit has already fired. Using publicly available intermediate checkpoints of open reasoning training runs (e.g., open-source R1-style RL/SFT runs on Qwen/Llama backbones) and, where checkpoints are unavailable, a controlled in-lab GRPO/SFT fine-tune of a small backbone, we trace across checkpoints (1) the step at which a linear latent-answer probe first correctly predicts the final answer within each trace (the internal commitment point), and (2) the length of the verbal trace. On GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and GPQA we test whether the commitment point moves earlier across training faster than the verbal trace shrinks, opening a growing commitment-to-trace gap that quantifies vestigial reasoning. We localize the latent-answer direction, validate it causally via truncate-at-commitment and activation patching, and track when this direction emerges over training. Finally we show the per-checkpoint commitment point yields a training-free, checkpoint-aware early-exit that shortens CoT with minimal accuracy loss. Our work reframes overthinking as the surface residue of a forming internalized-answer circuit and gives it a traceable developmental account.
Experiments: 1) Checkpoints and setup: Obtain a sequence of intermediate checkpoints spanning a reasoning fine-tune. Primary source: publicly released intermediate checkpoints of open R1-style SFT+RL (GRPO) runs on small backbones (e.g., Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B). Fallback (academic-lab-feasible): run our own controlled fine-tune of a small base model with SFT-then-GRPO on math, saving checkpoints at regular intervals. 2) Latent-answer probe per checkpoint: Segment each CoT into steps. At each step boundary decode the model's current implicit final answer via (a) logit-lens at the last position and (b) a trained linear probe on the residual stream predicting the eventual final answer token(s). Define the internal COMMITMENT POINT = earliest step after which the decoded answer matches the final answer and stays stable. Validate probe AUROC/accuracy per checkpoint on held-out problems. 3) Formation trajectory (core test): For each checkpoint, on GSM8K/MATH500/AIME/GPQA, record (i) mean commitment point (in fraction of trace), (ii) mean verbal trace length, (iii) accuracy. Test the central hypothesis: commitment point moves earlier across training faster than trace length shrinks, so the commitment-to-trace GAP (tokens generated after internal commitment) grows across checkpoints. Report gap trajectories; fit the emergence checkpoint where a stable, early commitment first appears. Compare against the behavioral expand-peak-contract length curve to show the gap is not visible from length alone. 4) Location and causal validation (per checkpoint, focus on late checkpoints): Localize the latent-answer direction via probe weights / difference-of-means and via activation patching; causally validate by truncating generation at the decoded commitment point and forcing termination, measuring accuracy retention vs. truncating at matched random earlier/later steps. Also patch the committed-answer representation from a late position into an earlier position and test whether it induces early answering. 5) Formation Tracing of the direction: Track when the latent-answer direction becomes decodable/sharp across checkpoints (probe accuracy vs. training step; principal-angle stability of the direction across checkpoints); test whether the direction is already weakly present in the base model (connecting to 'base models know how') and sharpens with training. Optionally, correlate its emergence with the RL reward-shaping phase. 6) Checkpoint-aware early-exit application: Use the per-checkpoint commitment point (probe stable + confident for k steps) as a training-free early-exit. Evaluate accuracy vs. mean tokens across checkpoints; compare to RCPD reactive exit, fixed truncation, and length-aware baselines. Metric: token-reduction-at-equal-accuracy, and whether the safe exit point tracks the traced commitment point. 7) Generalization: transfer probe/exit across datasets and (where available) model scales; test whether the commitment-to-trace gap widens monotonically or plateaus.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Publicly released intermediate reasoning checkpoints may be scarce or coarse; the in-lab controlled fine-tune fallback keeps the study feasible but limits scale to small backbones, so training-stage claims may not transfer to frontier models (an acknowledged boundary). The latent-answer probe is reliable mainly for extractable answers, restricting to math/multiple-choice. Probe accuracy itself changes across checkpoints, which could confound the commitment-point measurement; we control by using held-out validation, matched probe capacity per checkpoint, and reporting logit-lens (probe-free) commitment as a corroborating measure. The commitment-to-trace gap could reflect genuinely useful late verification rather than vestigial scaffold; the truncate-at-commitment causal test and hard-strata accuracy analysis address whether post-commitment tokens are actually redundant (a null here is itself informative). Activation patching across a forming circuit may be noisy at early checkpoints. Early-exit gains may not exceed strong reactive baselines, but the developmental/formation account of overthinking is the primary standalone contribution. Results may be training-recipe and model-family specific.
